title: AF-16 in Peritonitis Induced Sepsis
author: Annelie Tenhunen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdrsi56e

steps.title: Weigh the animal
steps.instruction: Measure and record the body weight of the animal.

steps.title: Premedicate animal
steps.instruction: Inject Zoletil Forte (Tiletamin/Zolazepam) 6 mg/kg plus Rompun (Xylazinklorid) 2.2 mg/kg intramuscularly into the neck muscle.

steps.title: Establish ear vein line and start Ringer infusion
steps.instruction: Place a peripheral venous catheter in an ear vein. Begin Ringer’s Acetate infusion at 30 ml/kg/h for the first hour, then reduce to 10 ml/kg/h until peritonitis induction.

steps.title: Position animal supine and induce anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the animal in supine position and give fentanyl 5–10 µg/kg intravenously for induction.

steps.title: Perform tracheostomy and start maintenance anesthesia
steps.instruction: Create a tracheostomy. Begin continuous infusion of ketamine 30 mg/kg/h, midazolam 0.1–0.4 mg/kg/h, and fentanyl 4 µg/kg/h dissolved in 2.5 % glucose solution. When anesthesia is confirmed by lack of reaction to painful stimulation of the front hooves, add rocuronium (Esmeron) 2.5 mg/kg/h.

steps.title: Insert catheters and surgical instrumentation
steps.instruction: Insert an arterial catheter into the right carotid artery, a pulmonary artery catheter, and a triple‑lumen central venous catheter via the right jugular vein. Place a PiCCO catheter in the right femoral artery. Perform a midline laparotomy, catheterize the urinary bladder, make a small caecal incision to collect feces (then close), and insert a large‑bore intra‑peritoneal drain before closing the abdominal wall.

steps.title: Prepare fecal slurry for peritonitis
steps.instruction: Weigh feces equal to 2 g per kg body weight, dissolve in 200 ml of 5 % glucose solution, and store at 38 °C until intraperitoneal instillation.

steps.title: Stabilize animal
steps.instruction: Allow the animal to stabilize for at least 30 minutes before further manipulations.

steps.title: Set mechanical ventilation
steps.instruction: Apply volume‑controlled ventilation with tidal volume 8 ml/kg, respiratory rate 25 /min, I:E ratio 1:2, FiO₂ 0.3, and PEEP 8 cmH₂O. Keep VT, I:E and PEEP constant. Adjust FiO₂ to keep PaO₂ > 10 kPa and adjust respiratory rate to keep PaCO₂ < 6.5 kPa.

steps.title: Record baseline measurements
steps.instruction: Obtain arterial and mixed‑venous blood gases, systemic and pulmonary pressures, cardiac output, heart rate, FiO₂, SaO₂, ETCO₂, plateau pressure, dynamic and static compliance, urinary output, extravascular lung water (EVLW) and stroke‑volume variation (SVV).

steps.title: Induce fecal peritonitis
steps.instruction: Remove the intra‑peritoneal drain, close the abdominal wall, and discontinue the Ringer’s Acetate infusion.

steps.title: Randomize animals
steps.instruction: Assign each animal to the AF‑16 group (n = 8) or control group (n = 8) using block randomization (4 × 4 sealed opaque envelopes); the research team remains blinded to allocation.

steps.title: Detect hemodynamic instability and begin monitoring
steps.instruction: Watch for onset of hemodynamic instability defined as a mean arterial pressure (MAP) drop lasting ≥5 minutes. At that moment, record arterial and mixed‑venous blood gases, systemic and pulmonary pressures, cardiac output, heart rate, FiO₂, SaO₂, ETCO₂, plateau pressure, dynamic and static compliance, and urine output hourly; measure SVV continuously; obtain EVLW and mixed‑venous blood gases now and every 3 hours thereafter.

steps.title: Administer AF‑16 or saline bolus
steps.instruction: For the AF‑16 group, give a bolus of 20 mg/kg AF‑16 (prepared as 50 mg/ml in 0.9 % saline) over 10 minutes, followed immediately by an infusion of 40 mg/kg over 50 minutes. The control group receives an equal volume of 0.9 % saline. Repeat the bolus dose at 4 hours and 8 hours after the first administration.

steps.title: Start antibiotic therapy
steps.instruction: Administer piperacillin/tazobactam 2 g intravenously every 8 hours, beginning after the onset of hemodynamic instability.

steps.title: Begin protocolized resuscitation
steps.instruction: Target MAP > 60 mmHg. Initiate fluid resuscitation with Ringer’s Acetate at 10 ml/kg/h.

steps.title: Apply fluid‑bolus algorithm
steps.instruction: If SVV > 15 % for ≥10 minutes, give a 150 ml bolus of Ringer’s Acetate. Repeat boluses until SVV stabilizes and MAP remains >60 mmHg, then reduce the continuous infusion to 5 ml/kg/h.

steps.title: Start insulin infusion if indicated
steps.instruction: When the animal is stable and SVV is maintained at 10 mmol/L, begin an insulin infusion of 1 U/ml at 1 ml/h.

steps.title: Euthanize animals
steps.instruction: Twenty hours after onset of hemodynamic instability, euthanize the animal with 100 mmol potassium chloride intravenously under deep anesthesia. If an animal reaches refractory shock and dies before the 20‑hour endpoint, give 100 mmol KCl IV at the terminal stage.

steps.title: Collect tissue samples
steps.instruction: Harvest lung tissue from five regions (apical‑medial, medial‑medial, caudal‑dorsal, caudal‑medial, caudal‑ventral) and samples of heart, liver, kidney, intestine, and skin. Immediately immerse all samples in 10 % buffered formalin for histology and for later wet‑to‑dry ratio determination.

steps.title: Determine wet‑to‑dry ratios
steps.instruction: Weigh each tissue sample, dry it in an oven at 50 °C until two consecutive weight measurements are identical, then record the dry weight for wet‑to‑dry ratio calculation.
